correctness.rationale: The natural-scale reflecting-absorbing boundary problem reduces exactly to an integral of (1-x)/D(x). For every mean budget, pointwise strict convexity of (1-x)/d+d/c^2 over a compact interval supplies a global unique profile, and exact elementary integrals yield the two phases. The explicit derivative calculation gives matching F,F′,F′′ and unequal one-sided third derivatives. Packaged checker passed exact algebra and independent quadrature/optimization comparisons; finite checks are supplementary, not a substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 full text gives the budgeted but unbounded optimal profile and generic variation, whereas the new theorem imposes simultaneous hard two-sided pointwise bounds and analytically classifies the upper-cap onset, complete optimal value and differentiability singularity. The 2023 primary text gives the general Itô first-passage integral but no bounded-resource optimum. The result is therefore a new constrained-design mathematical statement relative to the inspected primary sources, albeit based on well-known convex optimization and subject to priority risk from other literature.
